name: Ceramic bowl
description: A glazed soup bowl with a blue rim. Holds a serving of soup or water and can stand in embers to heat it.
notes: A turned bowl 130 mm across and 60 mm deep on a foot ring, ceramic-white with a paint-police-blue rim band. The box counts the air in the bowl.

name: Teacup
description: A thin china teacup with a loop handle.
notes: A turned teacup 90 mm across and 60 mm tall with a loop handle, 115 mm over the handle; ceramic-white. The tin cup rides on this model recoloured.

name: Tin cup
description: A pressed tin cup with a loop handle. It does not break when dropped.
notes: Rides on the ceramic_cup model with steel-grey for its one slot. A real tin cup is straighter-sided; the teacup shape is close enough at play distance. Its mass should differ from the shared model's 254 g; set it when the drafts are applied.

name: Coffee mug
description: A straight-sided ceramic mug with a loop handle, glazed red outside.
notes: A cylinder 84 mm across and 95 mm tall with a loop handle, 122 mm over the handle; paint-oxblood glaze outside, ceramic-white floor inside. Colour variants can recolour the glaze slot.

name: Dinner plate
description: A plain white china dinner plate.
notes: A turned plate 260 mm across and 22 mm high with a flat well and a sloping rim; ceramic-white. The box counts the air over the well. The tin and glass plates ride on this model recoloured; the meal tray rides on it too but deserves its own compartment-tray model later.

name: Tin plate
description: A pressed tin plate. Light, and it does not chip.
notes: Rides on the ceramic_plate model with steel-grey. Its mass should differ from the shared model's 375 g; set it when the drafts are applied.

name: Glass plate
description: A clear glass dinner plate.
notes: Rides on the ceramic_plate model with glass-clear; the tiles draw it opaque. Its mass should differ from the shared model's 375 g; set it when the drafts are applied.

name: Meal tray
description: A stainless tray for one meal.
notes: Rides on the ceramic_plate model with steel-stainless as a stand-in: a real meal tray is a rectangular tray with moulded compartments and wants its own model. Its mass should differ from the shared model's 375 g; set it when the drafts are applied.

name: Chopsticks
description: A pair of wooden chopsticks, lacquered red at the grip end.
notes: Two turned sticks 230 mm long tapering from 7 to 4 mm, lying side by side; lacquer-red grips, wood-birch tips. At the 2 mm grain the tips step coarsely.

name: Coffee pot
description: A glass carafe from a drip coffee maker, with a plastic collar and handle. It can sit on a fire to heat water.
notes: A turned glass carafe 150 mm across and 180 mm tall with a plastic-black collar, lid, pour lip and loop handle; 176 mm over the handle. The tiles draw glass-clear opaque.

name: Mesh colander
description: A stainless mesh bowl on a foot ring, with a handle at each side. Strains and sieves.
notes: A mesh bowl 220 mm across the rim and 108 mm tall on a foot ring with two flat side handles, 280 mm over them; mesh-black body with steel-stainless rim, foot and handles. The tiles draw the mesh opaque; it is see-through in game. The box counts the air inside. sieving is a new quality name.

name: Cutting board
description: A flat wooden board for chopping food on, with a hanging slot at one end.
notes: A birch board 410 by 250 by 20 mm lying flat with a 30 by 60 mm hanging slot built round with boxes, since compounds only add.

name: Cast-iron dutch oven
description: A heavy cast-iron pot on three short legs, with a flanged lid that holds hot coals and a wire bail. Bakes, roasts and stews over a fire.
notes: A camp oven: pot 260 mm across and 105 mm deep on three stub legs, flanged lid with a loop, two ears and a steel-grey wire bail arched over the top; iron-cast. The bail is a chain of 8 mm blocks so it stays visible at the 4 mm grain. baking is a new quality name for oven use.

name: Fork
description: A stainless steel table fork.
notes: A flat stainless fork 210 mm long with four tines, 3 mm thick; the bend of a real fork is left out. Several other small kitchen utensils ride on this model for now and each notes where its own shape differs.

name: Plastic fork
description: A white disposable plastic fork.
notes: Rides on the fork model with plastic-white. Its mass should differ from the shared model's 43 g; set it when the drafts are applied.

name: Corkscrew
description: A waiter's corkscrew with a fold-out spiral. Pulls corks from bottles.
notes: Rides on the fork model as a stand-in only: a corkscrew's handle and spiral need their own model. Its mass should differ from the shared model's 43 g; set it when the drafts are applied. opening is the existing quality for getting into containers.

name: Bottle opener
description: A flat steel bottle opener for crown caps.
notes: Rides on the fork model as a stand-in only: a flat opener with a hooked head needs its own model. Its mass should differ from the shared model's 43 g; set it when the drafts are applied.

name: Spork
description: A spoon with short tines cut into its tip.
notes: Rides on the fork model; a spork's bowled head would want its own model. Set its mass when the drafts are applied.

name: Foon
description: A spoon and fork in one piece, spoon at one end, fork at the other.
notes: Rides on the fork model; a double-ended utensil would want its own model. Set its mass when the drafts are applied.

name: Potato masher
description: A steel masher with a grid head on a long handle.
notes: Rides on the fork model as a stand-in only: a masher's grid head on a long handle needs its own model. Its mass should differ from the shared model's 43 g; set it when the drafts are applied.

name: Carving fork
description: A long two-pronged fork that holds a roast steady for carving.
notes: Rides on the fork model as a stand-in only: two long prongs on a riveted handle want their own model. Its mass should differ from the shared model's 43 g; set it when the drafts are applied.

name: Drinking glass
description: A straight-sided glass tumbler, taller than it is wide.
notes: A turned tumbler 80 mm across the rim and 160 mm tall with a 12 mm base; glass-clear, drawn opaque by the tiles.

name: Glass bowl
description: A clear, round-bottomed glass dish, deep enough for a serving of soup.
notes: A turned bowl 130 mm across and 65 mm deep; glass-clear, drawn opaque by the tiles.

name: Improvised oven
description: A large steel stockpot with a bed of pebbles and a wire trivet inside, so it bakes like an oven on a stove or hot coals.
notes: A pot 220 mm across and 150 mm deep, sooted coal-black at the base, with pebbles and a steel-bright trivet inside and its lid pushed aside; 250 mm over the side handles. The lid overhangs the rim to show the inside. baking is a new quality name.

name: Cast-iron pot
description: A heavy cast-iron pot, black outside and cream enamel inside, with a lug at each side.
notes: A turned pot 210 mm across and 120 mm tall with two lugs, 250 mm over them; iron-cast shell and paint-cream enamel lining.

name: Kettle
description: A stainless stovetop kettle with a spout and an arched handle.
notes: A turned body 170 mm across and 145 mm tall with a spout, lid and arched handle with a plastic-black grip; 188 mm over the spout.
